text: dsh-jev-goal-judge 是一个面向 DSH 目标轮次的判断插件：它在每轮结束时汇总助手文本、工具结果和此前轮次摘要，调用 Jev 评估目标是否完成、证据是否充分或是否反复遇到障碍。默认 shadow 模式只记录遥测；切换到 enforce 后，可在同一轮中提示 agent 验证完成情况或报告阻塞。它还提供 /jev-goal-stats 命令查看判断统计，适合希望减少无效目标轮次的 DSH 用户。使用时需配置 TypeSafe 或 OpenRouter 的密钥。

dsh-jev-goal-judge asks Jev to judge DSH goal rounds from bounded activity summaries, checking completion, evidence, and repeated blockers. Shadow mode logs results; enforce mode can prompt verification or a blocker report. It also provides /jev-goal-stats. Configure a TypeSafe or OpenRouter key.

能不能在完成目标前提醒 agent 再核对一次？
Help my DSH agent recognize when a goal is already complete.
Can I review progress and evidence at the end of each goal round?
dsh-jev-goal-judge 的功能「汇总目标轮次摘要」：该功能在会话事件中收集助手文本、工具调用结果和最近轮次结尾，并按配置限制摘要长度。目标轮次结束时提供摘要用于判断。
dsh-jev-goal-judge 的功能「判断目标完成情况」：该功能在轮次即将结束时向 Jev 提交目标和本轮摘要，评估完成程度与证据是否充分；答案缺失或置信度不足时返回不确定。
dsh-jev-goal-judge 的功能「提示核验完成或报告阻塞」：启用 enforce 模式且判断通过阈值后，插件向当前 agent 发送固定模板提示，要求核验目标完成情况或报告持续障碍。
dsh-jev-goal-judge 的功能「查看轮次判断统计」：在 DSH commands 服务可用时注册 /jev-goal-stats，读取遥测并汇总判断数、结论分布、延迟和估算成本。
dsh-jev-goal-judge 会把目标内容和轮次摘要发送到所选的 Jev 服务进行判断；遥测记录保存在本地 telemetry.jsonl。 (见 src/jev.ts:150-154)

dsh-jev-goal-judge README · dsh-jev-goal-judge：> **A Jev progress judgment between DeepSeek Harness goal rounds — for about two cents per thousand rounds.**
>
> dsh's goal-round driver continues rounds on a counter, not on evidence: `roundsStarted < maxGoalRounds` is the only stop check, and the tool policy lets a real blocker burn three full rounds before `blocked` is accepted. This plugin puts one bounded [Jev](https://typesafe.ai) typed-decision call at each round boundary: when a round's turn is about to close, the judge asks whether the objective looks achieved, evidenced, or stuck on the same obstacle — and in enforce mode steers a fixed-template nudge back into the **same turn**, so a round that would only re-discover what the judge already saw never runs.

dsh-jev-goal-judge README · dsh-jev-goal-judge：**What it does, in one breath:** at `agent/turn-stopping` of every goal round, one Jev fan-out (`achieved`/`evidence` nouls + a `progress` score + a `sameObstacle` noul + an `action` choice, ≤16k chars of state, ~$0.00002) judges the closing round against the objective; a confident *achieved-and-evidenced* verdict steers *"verify and mark it complete now"*, a confident *same-obstacle-again* verdict steers *"report blocked or change approach"* — and everything else, including every error, timeout, cooldown, and low-confidence answer, stays silent and leaves stock driver behavior untouched.

dsh-jev-goal-judge README · Why this exists：| Stock behavior | Cost |
| --- | --- |
| `roundsStarted >= maxGoalRounds` is the **only** stop check | every round below the limit runs, unconditionally |
| The model-facing tool policy accepts `blocked` only after the **same blocker persists across three rounds** | a real blocker donates two extra full turns to proving it is boring |
| Nothing checks whether work already done satisfies the objective | an agent that finishes but never calls `update_goal complete` donates a whole round to re-discovering that |

dsh-jev-goal-judge README · Why this exists：Each wasted round is a full agent turn of tokens. This plugin makes the boundary between rounds a *measured* decision instead of a counter — the same System-1-over-rules move `dsh-jev-interceptor` made for tool-call gating, applied to the goal loop.

dsh-jev-goal-judge README · How it works：```
session/event stream ──► RoundObserver ──► bounded per-round digest
                                                │
agent/turn-stopping (serial) ──────────────────►┤ goal active+armed? closing turn is round N≥1?
                                                ▼

dsh-jev-goal-judge README · How it works：- **The seam.** `agent/turn-stopping` is the documented serial extension point for objecting to a turn close; it runs *before* the driver queues the next round on idle, so there is no race. `steer()` submits to the **next-step** boundary — the driver's competing-message listener only flags `nextTurn` inserts, so a judge note can never be mistaken for a human interjection and can never pause the goal.
- **The judge.** One call, five fixed questions. Instruction strings are constants; transcript text lives only in the `state` data field, so tool output can never rewrite what is being asked. Routing is deterministic: the noul thresholds decide, the `action` choice only breaks ties — a threshold change replays exactly over logged answers.
- **The savings.** A steered extra step that ends in `update_goal complete` means the driver never queues the next round at all: **the whole round is saved.** A steered *"report blocked"* that lands converts three rounds of blocker evidence into one.

dsh-jev-goal-judge README · Safety model (the part you should actually read)：- **Judge, not gatekeeper.** v1 never mutates goal state — no `block`, no `pause`, no `complete`, no `disarm`. The only actuator is `agent.steer()` with a fixed-template advisory note. The agent and the human stay sovereign; the driver's own policies stay in force.
- **Fail-open everywhere.** No key, cooldown, timeout, parse mismatch, or sub-floor confidence degrades to stock behavior. The plugin can shorten a goal; it can never extend, block, or widen one.
- **Bounded by construction.** Assistant tail ≤ 6000 chars, final message ≤ 2000, tool entries ≤ 40, previous finals ≤ 2 × 1500 — comfortably inside Jev's 32k state budget. Provider limits: one retry on 429/529/5xx inside the remaining budget, cooldown after consecutive failures, concurrency cap.
- **Steer budgets.** At most 2 `verify-complete` and 1 `report-blocked` nudges per goal: the judge can never talk more than the rounds it saves. Notes are parameterized by round numbers only — no model- or Jev-generated text is ever echoed into a prompt.
- **Shadow first.** The default mode records every judgment to telemetry (`<DSH_HOME>/dsh-jev-goal-judge/tel

text: dsh-jev-goal-judge README · Configure：Everything is a config field — timeouts, cooldown, concurrency, digest bounds, every threshold, steer budgets (see `Config` in `src/config.ts`). Notable defaults:

dsh-jev-goal-judge README · Configure：- `mode: shadow` — nothing is steered until you say so.
- `minRoundsForBlocked: 2` — the blocked nudge needs at least one prior round to compare.
- `verifyCompleteMax: 2`, `reportBlockedMax: 1` — the per-goal steer budgets.
- Provider endpoints: TypeSafe direct (`api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone`, model `jev-latest`) or OpenRouter (`openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions`, model `~typesafe/jev-latest`). The key resolves through the dsh credential seam (`~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml`), then the launch environment, then ambient env.

dsh-jev-goal-judge README · Cost：Jev 1.13: $0.042 per million input tokens, output free. A judgment call carries 500–2000 input tokens, once per **round** (not per tool call): **~$0.00002–0.00008 per round**. A 12-round goal costs less than a thousandth of a dollar to judge end to end.

dsh-jev-goal-judge README · What this plugin deliberately does not do：- No direct `ctx.goals` mutations — advisory steering only, v1 and by default.
- No round extension, model routing, compaction, or cross-goal memory — one seam, done properly.
- No free-form generated text in steer notes — fixed templates, round numbers only.
